title.value: Photoredox/Copper Dual-Catalyzed Phosphorothiolation of Propargylic Derivatives for the Switchable Synthesis of S‑Alkyl, S‑Vinyl and S‑Allenyl Phosphorothioates

abstract.value: Herein, we report a photoredox/copper dual-catalyzed selective phosphorothiolation of propargylic derivatives from easily accessible [P(O)SH] compounds. This reaction provides a general, mild and versatile procedure to synthesize a variety of synthetically useful S-alkyl, S-vinyl and S-allenyl phosphorothioates selectively from the same set of simple starting materials. P hosphorothioates containing a phosphorus−sulfur singlebond (P−S) are widely found in many pharmaceutical and agrochemical molecules (Scheme 1a).1 Traditional methods, such as Michaelis−Arbuzov-type reaction, for the synthesis of phosphorothioates usually required thiols as the starting materials, which might suffer from high temperature, toxicity, and moisture sensitivity of reagents, thus resulting in harsh reaction conditions, complicated operation, and limited substrates (Scheme 1b, top).2 By contrast, S-hydrogen phosphorothioates [P(O)SH]3−7 and their salts,8 regardless of presynthesized or generated in situ, have been developed as an important synthon in phosphorothiolation processes under mild reaction conditions. As a result, this readily available, stable and low-toxicity [P(O)SH] reagent in phosphorothiolation reactions with olefins,5 terminal alkynes6 or via 1,5- hydrogen atom transfer (1,5-HAT) process7 and so on3,4,8 provide an important alternative for the synthesis of a variety of high-value phosphorothioates (Scheme 1b, bottom). However, the transformations involving [P(O)SH] reagents are still underdeveloped; therefore, achieving structurally diverse phosphorothioates from [P(O)SH] compounds remains a desirable yet challenging goal. Propargylic derivatives, a kind of redox-active substrate, could be easily activated to generate propargyl species and its tautomeric allenyl species.9,10 Benefiting from the extraordinary reaction characteristics of propargyl radicals, major advancements have been achieved in the transformation of propargyl derivatives into functionalized propargylic derivatives9 or allenes4,10 via metal-catalyzed coupling reactions. However, these elegant works are mostly limited to the intrinsic two-electron mechanism involving an oxidative addition-transmetalation-reductive elimination process, while examples involving a visible-light-induced through single electron transfer (SET) process are scarce.9d,10j In continuation of our efforts in copper-catalyzed phosphorothiolation with [P(O)SH] reagents,3e,6b,7 we speculated that the reactive propargyl radicals and their tautomeric allenyl radicals could be generated from propargylic derivatives via an SET process which might be suitable for the construction of propargylic or allenylic phosphorothioates. On the other hand, we doubt that whether the highly reactive allenyl radicals could interact with oxygen to generate alkenyl radical11 which might also be able to couple with [P(O)SH] reagents to produce vinylic phosphorothioates (Scheme 1c).
